findings.evidence: Diff: `exact congrFun (congrArg Equiv.toFun (LinearEquiv.mapProjectivization_symm e.toLinearEquiv)) p`, and the matching lines in the refl and trans lemmas. Mathlib already has the explicit bridges: `mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Basic.lean:295 theorem toLinearEquiv_symm` and `:330 theorem trans_toLinearEquiv`.
findings.fix: Add one bridge lemma, `toEquiv_mapProjectivization : e.mapProjectivization.toEquiv = e.toLinearEquiv.mapProjectivization`, and rewrite with it together with the explicit Mathlib lemmas `ContinuousLinearEquiv.toLinearEquiv_symm` and `ContinuousLinearEquiv.trans_toLinearEquiv`. Alternatively, restore the previous `ext p; induction p using ind with | h v hv => simp` proofs, which go through the public `mapProjectivization_mk` simp lemmas.
findings.issue: `ContinuousLinearEquiv.mapProjectivization_symm` is closed by `congrFun (congrArg Equiv.toFun (LinearEquiv.mapProjectivization_symm e.toLinearEquiv)) p`. This only typechecks because the kernel silently unfolds three things: the `Homeomorph` structure update to `Equiv.toFun`, `e.symm.toLinearEquiv` to `e.toLinearEquiv.symm`, and the Homeomorph `.symm` application. None of this is commented. The same pattern appears in `mapProjectivization_refl` (line ~177), which needs `(ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl K V).toLinearEquiv` to be definitionally `LinearEquiv.refl K V`, and in `mapProjectivization_trans` (line ~191), which needs `(e₁.trans e₂).toLinearEquiv` to be definitionally `e₁.toLinearEquiv.trans e₂.toLinearEquiv`. It also appears in the `continuous_invFun` field of `ContinuousLinearEquiv.mapProjectivization` (line ~141), where `h` states `e.symm.toLinearEquiv.mapProjectivization` but is proved by a lemma about `e.toLinearEquiv.symm`.

summary: The prior `change`, undocumented `rfl` and lemma-free `simp only` are now gone or commented. The new `ContinuousLinearEquiv.mapProjectivization` lemmas replace robust `ext; induction; simp` proofs with `congrFun (congrArg Equiv.toFun …)` terms that rely on uncommented definitional unfolding between wrappers.
